text.p: Two soccer friendlies between clubs from the Greek Cypriot community and the Turkish Cypriot community, the first in more than 40 years on divided Cyprus, have been called off.
"There was a conflict in the procedure of organising the two matches. The matches have been suspended for a later date," a Greek Cypriot F.A. source told Reuters on Monday.
The friendlies were to be held at the prompting of international football federation FIFA.

Greek Cypriot team AEL was due to play Turkish Cypriot Genclerbirligi in the southern Greek Cypriot controlled areas on Thursday. The rematch was due to take place a week later in the Turkish-held north.
"As far as we are concerned, there is no need for a cancellation. We want the matches to take place and we are ready for them," said Omer Adal, Turkish Cypriot football federation chairman.
Cyprus F.A. sources told Reuters the problems hinged on the content of a letter sent by the Turkish Cypriots to FIFA complaining about a phrase used by the Greek Cypriots in their correspondence.

The Greek Cypriots described Lapithos, the town where the rematch was due to take place as "Turkish occupied", reflecting the official Greek Cypriot line relating to the Turkish invasion of the island in 1974.
The Turkish Cypriots, according to the same source, responded by stating there were no Turkish occupied areas.
